- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.3) — raise forecast floor by 5–10%.
- Avoid overshooting after recent spikes — cap forecast 3–5 days post-spike at 1–2% below peak.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecasts are above 10% above history mean, reduce next forecast by 10–15%.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 2–3% if sentiment is high and recent price action is flat or declining.
- If sentiment is rising and price is trending up, delay forecast peak by 1–2 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is falling and price is trending down, delay forecast trough by 1–2 days to avoid premature bottoming.
